questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had already gone on exchange in my 5th semester and I originally wanted to go to Australia. Due to Corona it was not possible so I chose to go to England instead with my friend. We chose Newcastle because it was not a common place for people from KU to go to and we wanted a local experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Considering I already went on exchange once, I did not have expectations other than doing a different semester in the UK and to travel around. If I had been alone or this had been my first exchange, it would not have met my expectations at all.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was definitely a challenge. Since Newcastle had not exchanged any students with Copenhagen since 2017 every piece of information we could find were outdated. Furthermore, Newcastle was not set up for the online mobility platform that KU was, so it was quite difficult to gather the documents needed to apply.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We hardly did not receive any information. As Newcastle does quite a lot of exchange with Chinese and american students, they had had a information week a couple of weeks before we got there. Since we came right before school started everything had already happened. The staff at the school were very helpful, although we had to seek all the information out we needed ourselves.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: In contrast to the institution I visited my 5th semester, Newcastle had not planned anything that was of help to me and my friend.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: This was first hand one of the things I was very pleased about that was offered. My previous exchange the school was not helpful at all in the housing of their incoming exchange students. Newcastle just had a form we had to fill out and then we were placed in student accommodation. It was possible to choose quite a range of different options in regards to payments and facilities available.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a kitchen at my student accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very crucial to be aware of the fact that in the UK it is only the first (and sometimes 2nd years) that live on campus. The rest finds housing / apartments around the city on their own. This meant that I was placed with 6 18 year old british students that had never lived outside their parents home. This was very frustrating in terms of me being seven years old than them in regards to noise, cleaning etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We got all the classes we wanted.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite easy and online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had to look at the student web page for exam information. We chose in terms of what exams were the easiest to pass.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% succesfull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose modules that have the easier exams, such as essays etc. This will make the exchange so much better so that you do not have to sit in the library your last month to memorize the entire class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The teachers were good, the classes were good. Overall a good academic experience.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: We had both a masters class (4th year) and a freshers class (1st year). The levels of difficulties were different to the british students but to us it was almost the same, because out awareness of the British legal system was less of that of the British students. It was a good academic level overall.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more listening and taking notes, which I quite like. Hardly any presentations or assignments during the semester. We only had one or two things we needed to attend and do doing the semester which made traveling and free planning a lot easier.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Legal Institutions and Methods, Law and Literature and Foundations of Business and Commercial law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of the above classes. I would recommend Legal institutions and Methods because of the introduction to the British legal system overall. I learned a lot of the country that I was doing an exchange in. The two other courses were also good and did not require a lot of work doing the semester. Furthermore the examination in the two latter courses were 100% essay which made the semester easier to pass.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was quite expensive to travel with train which we did a lot to see the country and area we lived in.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cost of living is cheaper than in CPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We did not attend very much. People were very young.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Clubs, sport clubs and academic opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Since we had already had one exchange experience where we attended much of the School activities this exchange for us was more about traveling and going out on the weekends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely go about and see the areas around Newcastle. Travel to Scotland and drive around. Go to football games in St. James park.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. The Geordies are friendly people, although the are quite different from Danish people in regards to how the dress.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out and talk to people at bars and clubs. It is very easy to meet people in Newcastle.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The English are not cold when they go out which means that the do not wear jackets to the club. This means that there is not wardrobe at the clubs and we were running freezing most of the time we went out.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nightlife and the football life of Newcastle.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do not go unless you are doing an exchange with a friend. I would not recommend going to Newcastle if it is your first exchange because you are on your own in regards to socializing etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: We got our acceptance letter so late that we almost cancelled the exchange. You got to have a lot of patience if you want to go to Newcastle.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Traveling around the UK and meeting a lot of locals that you would not meet in cities such as London.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That we were on our own in terms of what we wanted to do with the exchange. It was challenging at first but turned out that the freedom of not getting much information and help meant that we could go about as we wanted to in terms of planning our weeks in Newcastle.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Overall it was a great experience, but I would not recommend it unless you have already previously done and exchange or if you don't know anyone at the institution.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
